title: Anthropic Claude hits a two-phase outage across claude.ai, Code, and Cowork
subtitle: The Monday incident opened at 14:00 UTC, was partially mitigated at 14:36, then re-escalated at 15:00 to block new chats, sign-ins, and file uploads before full restoration.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Anthropic's status page opened an incident at 14:21 UTC on Monday, September 29, reporting elevated error rates across claude.ai, Claude Code, Claude Cowork, and the Claude API. The errors began at 14:00 UTC. Downdetector recorded roughly 18,335 outage reports at peak, against a normal baseline of about 10. Anthropic partially mitigated the first failure at 14:36, and existing conversations mostly resumed; sign-ins continued to fail. At 15:00 UTC the company opened a second failure that blocked new chats, voice conversations, Claude Code and Cowork sessions, subscription purchases, and file uploads. Full restoration was reported around 17:12 UTC. Anthropic said some messages sent during the outage window were not saved.

Two-phase outages — where a first fix reveals a second failure — are diagnostically informative. They usually indicate a load or state issue that a partial mitigation shifted but did not resolve, so recovery traffic hits the still-broken path. The specific surfaces that broke second (auth, purchase, file upload) suggest a shared identity or storage dependency behind the split, not the model inference layer. Anthropic has had a run of these in 2026: the August 25 Mythos-Fable-Opus multi-model outage, the July 10 usage-limit reset failure, and now this one. Each has been shorter than the last, which is a real improvement, but the customer concentration in the leaked IPO prospectus is a reminder that a two-hour outage of Claude Code is a two-hour outage for a large share of Anthropic revenue.

The timing is also relevant. The outage landed the same day the S-1 leak was making rounds, one day before OpenAI's DevDay, and on top of a US federal AI portal launch. A significant slice of enterprise developers experiencing 'you cannot sign in to Claude Code' on that specific Monday will remember it — Anthropic's postmortem, when it publishes, will need to be more specific than usual to hold the trust it built with the science-model launches earlier in the month.

For learners: reliability is a feature of AI products in a way that many teams still under-invest in. Every hour of Claude Code downtime pushes a developer to Cursor, ChatGPT, or Copilot, and switching costs are asymmetric — a habit swap is easier than a habit return. When you build on top of a frontier lab's API, read its historical status page before you commit to it, and design your product for at least two provider fallbacks. The right question at architecture review is not 'which model is best?' but 'what does my product do at 15:00 UTC when the model I picked returns 500 for 90 minutes?'
